title: Practical electronics basics
summary: GPIO, logic levels, pull resistors, ADC, PWM, buses, grounds, and drivers.
body:
GPIO and logic levels

A GPIO is a small logic signal. HIGH is near the board logic supply and LOW is near ground. ESP GPIO is normally 3.3 V logic; do not assume 5 V tolerance. An output cannot safely supply a motor, relay coil, pump, valve, heater, or speaker.

Inputs

An unconnected input floats and may change randomly. A pull-up holds it HIGH until a switch connects it to ground; a pull-down does the opposite. Active-low modules report the asserted state as LOW. Debounce filters contact transitions but does not repair bad wiring.

ADC and PWM

An ADC converts voltage into a number. Keep the GPIO inside its permitted range; a divider scales higher voltages. Calibration and averaging improve useful accuracy. PWM switches rapidly; duty cycle controls a suitable LED, fan input, or motor driver. It is not a true analog supply.

Buses

  • I2C: shared SDA/SCL, device addresses, usually pull-ups.
  • SPI: shared clock/data plus chip-select per device.
  • UART: cross TX to RX and share ground.
  • I2S: digital audio clocks and data.

Drivers and ground

A driver translates GPIO into load current/voltage. Low-voltage systems usually require a shared ground so signals have the same reference. Isolation modules can differ; follow their datasheet.

title: Electrical and equipment safety
summary: Safe boundaries for GPIO, relays, motors, pumps, heaters, and mains equipment.
body: ELMA-IoT wiring diagrams describe controller-side signals. They are not approval to work on hazardous voltage.

Never drive loads directly

Use a rated relay module, MOSFET driver, H-bridge, or contactor interface. Add flyback protection for inductive DC loads unless the driver includes it. Size wiring, connectors, fuses, and supplies for normal and fault current.

Mains and high energy

Mains heaters, pumps, compressors, and gate motors require suitable enclosures, isolation, earthing, over-current protection, emergency disconnection, and local-code compliance. Keep exposed low-voltage prototypes away from mains.

Fail-safe design

  • Choose the safe output state for boot, disconnect, sensor failure, and restart.
  • Use independent hardware limits for motion and over-temperature.
  • Limit motor and pump runtime.
  • Test unplugged sensors and network loss deliberately.
  • Do not rely on MQTT or a phone notification as the only safety mechanism.

title: Building devices from multiple peripherals
summary: Combine values, decisions, timing, actions, status, and MQTT into robust devices.
body:
Think in roles

Observe → decide → trigger → act → verify → report

A sensor observes. Compare decides. Rising/Falling Edge turns a changing Boolean into one Flow pulse. A relay acts. A state block verifies. MQTT reports.

Progressive example

  1. Temperature + relay: one threshold demonstrates value and action wiring.
  2. Two thresholds: ON above 30 °C and OFF below 27 °C prevents chatter.
  3. Timing: Delay, Cooldown, or explicit state paths protect against rapid commands.
  4. MQTT: Timer produces periodic Flow while the live value supplies payload.
  5. Availability: supported sensor Available/Error values guard actions and create alarms.

One board, many roles

Name every slot by physical purpose, keep topics unique, and group independent automations. Shared buses may share lines only when address and chip-select rules are satisfied.

title: How to think about Logics
summary: Translate real requirements into values, Boolean decisions, Flow events, and actions.
body:
The sentence method

Write: When X happens, check Y, then do Z. “When” becomes an event, edge, or timer; “check” becomes a Boolean condition; “do” becomes an action with a white Flow input.

Data is not execution

A temperature value connected to Compare updates Result. It does not fire a relay. Use Rising Edge, Falling Edge, IF, Branch, Timer, or another Flow-producing block.

Temperature → Compare A (> 30) → Result → Rising Edge Value
Rising Edge Out → Relay ON In

Enable and hysteresis

(Temperature > 30) AND SystemEnabled → Rising Edge → Fan ON
Temperature < 27 → Rising Edge → Fan OFF

Between 27 and 30 °C the previous output state remains unchanged.

Runtime limits

Firmware graphs support at most 64 nodes, 128 connections, and a 32 KiB payload. Timing is greater than zero and at most 86,400 seconds. Repeat count is 1–128. Incompatible types, cycles, missing required ports, and unsupported adapters are rejected.

title: State, edges, timers, delays, and repeat
summary: Use time and state without producing continuous or duplicated actions.
body:
Level versus transition

A Boolean may remain True for minutes. Rising Edge fires once when False becomes True; Falling Edge fires once on the reverse transition; On Change fires on either.

Timing blocks

BlockImplemented behaviorUse
DelayOne pulse after Seconds.Turn off later.
TimerPeriodic pulses using Seconds; can be enabled.Telemetry.
RepeatCount pulses, first immediately; active retriggers ignored.Three alerts.
DebounceWait for a quiet period.Mechanical input.
CooldownPass one, suppress others for Seconds.Alarm rate limit.

Persistence

Defaults, positions, connections, groups, and mode are stored and embedded. Runtime readings do not replace project defaults.
